ranking.note: Raised to P1: removes the cs_main dependency from index sync and fixes startup/reindex race conditions, and is the prerequisite for out-of-process indexing (#10102) and shared rescan logic (#15719) — exactly the refactor class the category treats as high value.
Raised to P1: txindex corruption and disk I/O failures currently surface as 'transaction does not exist' over RPC/REST — the category's worst case of an index silently returning wrong answers.
Kept P2: same class of problem as #35728 (silent read failures) but centred on dbwrapper/coins, so its in-category benefit is indirect.
Placed ahead of #26966 because it is the stated foundation work that parallel sync builds on.

inconsistencies: #35728 and #34132 both attack silent read-error masking (corrupted/failed reads treated as 'missing'). #35728 is the index-scoped fix and should be reviewed first; #34132's fatal-on-read-failure policy may subsume or conflict with the RPC-level throwing, so the two need to be reconciled rather than merged independently.
Chain: #34489 (batched index writes) is explicitly extracted as foundation for #26966 (parallel index sync), and #34489 itself depends on merged #34897. Review in the order #34489 → #26966.

#36002 (txindex in pruned mode) and #36480 (txospenderindex compact keys, 'prepares for pruned mode') both build on the key-format change merged in #35531 and both refactor the shared block-sequencing helpers; they will overlap in txindex code and should be sequenced, with #36002 first as the one delivering user-visible capability.

#24230 (indexes stop using node internal types / cs_main) and #35474 (move index ownership from globals into NodeContext) are overlapping decoupling refactors touching the same ownership and access paths; #24230 carries the correctness fixes and downstream dependents and should set the direction.
result.notes: Original assessments clustered seven of ten PRs in P2; the band split here separates the two correctness/lock-dependency items (#24230, #35728) from the feature and performance work, and keeps the two pure-housekeeping refactors in P3/P4.
